newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras wants to charge U.S. for army base.
newsitem.headline: Honduras wants to charge U.S. for army base.

text.p: President Carlos Roberto Reina proposed on Tuesday that the United States be charged for using the Palmerola army base in central Honduras.
Reina told a news conference that Honduras should revise a bilateral 1954 treaty that allows the United States to station troops in this Central American country.
About 500 U.S. troops have been posted at Palmerola since 1983.
"I don't think it would be any indignity to charge money for Palmerola," Reina said. "I think that Spain has done it, that France has done it."
Reina said the idea has not yet been formally proposed to the United States, nor a price set.
"To me, we have to revise at the negotiating table an agreement that was established in the context of the Cold War," Reina said.

In the 1980s, Honduras was home to one of the world's largest CIA operations and the site of annual U.S. Army manoeuvres in the U.S. anti-communist effort in neighbouring El Salvador, Nicaragua and Guatemala.
Top Honduran army officers recently brought up the proposal to charge the United States for Palmerola.
